::api-operation{method="POST" path="/v1/businesses/{biz}/subscriptions/{sub}/change"}
#docs
## Path parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `biz` | `string` | **yes** | Business id (biz_…) |
| `sub` | `string` | **yes** | Subscription id (sub_…) |

## Headers

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Idempotency-Key` | `string` | no | Safely retry writes — repeats return the original response. If a write FAILED after it had already taken effect, that failure is what repeats: the key is spent, and a new attempt needs a new key. |

## Body

The request body is **required**.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `coupon_code` | `string` | no | A coupon to apply AS PART OF this change. Applied inside the change's own transaction, BEFORE its proration invoice is raised — so the proration is discounted, which is the intended behaviour. Posting it as a separate call afterwards bills the proration at list price. `POST …/estimate` takes the same field and previews the same result. |
| `coupon_ids` | `array of string` | no | The same coupon as `coupon_code`, as a list. A subscription carries ONE discount at a time, so more than one entry is refused (400), as is a `coupon_code` naming a different coupon. |
| `manual_discount` | `object` | no | A manual discount to apply as part of this change — same shape `POST …/subscriptions/{sub}/manual_discount` takes, minus `note`, so one screen sends one body shape to the preview and the booking. `duration` defaults to `forever`. |
| `manual_discount.type` | `string` | **yes** | The discount type. One of `percent`, `amount`. |
| `manual_discount.value` | `number` | **yes** | 1–100 for `percent`; minor units for `amount`. |
| `manual_discount.duration` | `string` | no | How long the discount lasts. One of `one_time`, `forever`. |
| `remove_discount` | `boolean` | no | Remove the subscription's active discount (coupon or manual) as part of this change, inside its transaction and BEFORE the proration invoice is raised — so that invoice bills without it. With `coupon_code` or `manual_discount` it swaps the discount in one edit. On the estimate it prices the same order. |
| `changes` | `array of object` | no | Existing items to change. |
| `changes.item` | `string` | **yes** | The subscription item's id (si_…). |
| `changes.price` | `string` | no | The new price's id (a slug id, e.g. `pro-monthly-usd`). |
| `changes.quantity` | `integer` | no | The new quantity. |
| `changes.unit_price_minor` | `integer` | no | Custom price override (flat/per-unit only), minor units |
| `adds` | `array of object` | no | Items to ATTACH by this same call — priced exactly as `POST …/items` prices them, including plan-scoped differential resolution. A recurring add is prorated to the remaining term (the full term when this edit resets it); a one-time add is charged in full. Cadence is validated against the POST-change plan cycle, so an added yearly add-on is legal in the same call that moves the plan to its yearly price. |
| `adds.price` | `string` | **yes** | The price's id (a slug id, e.g. `pro-monthly-usd`). |
| `adds.quantity` | `integer` | no | The quantity. Defaults to `1`. |
| `adds.unit_price_minor` | `integer` | no | Custom price override (flat/per-unit only), minor units |
| `removes` | `array of string` | no | Subscription item ids to DETACH by this same call — each credits the unused time exactly as `DELETE …/items/:id` does (a one-time item is credited nothing), into the same document as the rest of the edit. No line ever bills an item the same call removes. A mandatory add-on of the POST-change plan is refused; the same item may not appear in both `changes` and `removes`. |
| `at` | `string · ISO-8601` | no | Backdate the change (proration as of this instant) |
| `reset_term` | `boolean` | no | Restart the term today and charge the FULL new-term price. Default false, and a SAME-CADENCE plan swap does NOT reset without it — a billing-frequency change always does, with or without it. |
| `prorate` | `boolean` | no | False suppresses the PRORATED credit and charge. On a term reset the full new-term charge is not a prorated artefact and still happens — only the unused-time credit is dropped, so there is no free term. Omitted = the business rule for the change's direction (`billing_rules_config.upgrade_proration` or `downgrade_proration`; unset, prorated). A value sent here applies to this change in either direction. A longer billing period is an upgrade and a shorter one a downgrade; on the same period the recurring amount per month decides. |
| `timing` | `string` | no | `now` applies the change; `end_of_term` schedules it for the current term end (the trial end in a trial) and returns `scheduled_change`. Omitted = the business rule for the change's direction (`billing_rules_config.upgrade_timing` or `downgrade_timing`); unset, `now`. Omitted with any of `at`, `reset_term`, `prorate`, `invoice_immediately`, `metadata` or a discount = `now` when the rule allows it. A timing the rule does not allow is refused (400). A change at the end of the term cannot carry those fields (400 names them). One of `now`, `end_of_term`. |
| `invoice_immediately` | `boolean` | no | Invoicing options: true raises the proration invoice now and collects it; false queues the same lines as unbilled charges, folded into the next renewal invoice (where tax and account credits are applied). OMITTED resolves the business setting `default_invoice_immediately` (Settings &gt; Billing LogIQ &gt; Update subscription), which is off by default — so omitting this queues unbilled charges unless the business turned it on. Pass true explicitly to invoice now regardless of that setting. Credits (downgrade / term-reset) are issued immediately either way. |
| `priced_at` | `string · ISO-8601` | no | `priced_at` from `POST …/estimate`. Send it only with `quote`, on a change applied now without `at` (else 400). The change is booked at this instant when it is at most 15 minutes old and no more than 5 seconds ahead of the server clock, so the unused-time credit is the one the estimate showed; otherwise it is priced at the moment of the call. |
| `quote` | `string` | no | `quote` from `POST …/estimate`. Only on a change applied now (`timing: now`, or omitted when the business rule resolves to now) without `at`; otherwise 400. The change is priced again with this body and refused (409, `param: quote`) when any amount differs from the estimate, or when the subscription renewed after `priced_at`. Nothing is booked. Omitted, no check is made. |

## Response

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `object` | `string` | The object type; always `subscription_change`. One of `subscription_change`. |
| `subscription` | `string` | The subscription id. |
| `proration_invoice` | `object` | The invoice that the change raised, or null if it raised none. |
| `credit_note` | `object` | The credit note that the change raised, or null if it raised none. |
| `unbilled_charges` | `array of object` | Charges that were queued instead of invoiced, or null if none were queued. |
| `timing` | `string` | When the change takes effect. One of `now`, `end_of_term`. |
| `credit_refunds` | `array of object` | Only with `billing_rules_config.downgrade_credit: refund` and a credit to refund. |
| `scheduled_change` | `object` | The scheduled change when `timing` is `end_of_term`, else null. |

## Status codes

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` | Applied (with proration invoice if any), or scheduled for the term end (`scheduled_change`) |
| `400` | Invalid change |
| `409` | Refused by the business's plan-change gate (`error.code` = `invoices_unpaid`), or a concurrent write |

#request
```bash [Request]
curl -X POST "$TMBILLING_URL/v1/businesses/biz_XXXXXXXXXXXX01/subscriptions/sub_XXXXXXXXXXXX01/change" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TMBILLING_API_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "coupon_code": "welcome-10",
    "remove_discount": false
  }'
```
